acceptance_test_matrix: Config semantic coverage: every existing /api/config/* route is exercised with domain=equities and domain=crypto, asserting runtimeConfigVersion, graphId, live config, partition state, and venue list are domain-correct.

Diagnostics semantic coverage: every existing /api/diagnostics/* route is exercised with domain=equities and domain=crypto, asserting runtime and partition metadata do not leak identifiers across domains.
Default compatibility coverage: omitted domain parameter continues to match existing equities behavior.
Edge-case coverage: unknown or malformed domain follows existing API validation or domain-resolution behavior without adding mutation or new endpoint paths.
Isolation coverage: back-to-back equities and crypto requests remain request-scoped and do not leak graph IDs, venues, identifiers, live config, runtimeConfigVersion, or partition state.
Playwright coverage: selector-switch flow visits both equities and crypto and verifies API-backed or rendered config/diagnostics metadata changes rather than only checking visual state.

Configured QA gate coverage: ./gradlew :app-api:test, ./qa/smoke.sh, ./qa/regression.sh, and npm --prefix ui run test:e2e provide controller-level parity, selector switching, and repo smoke/regression evidence.
assumptions: Domain selection is query-param based with ?domain=crypto or ?domain=equities, and omitted domain remains backward-compatible with existing equities behavior.
Crypto runtime metadata already exists in approved runtime sources such as Redis hot views or existing historical-read services and does not require new persistence.
This feature is a compact read-only parity pass and must not introduce endpoint expansion, config mutation, runtime backfill, or app-api write behavior.
Playwright selector-switch coverage can be authored under tests/ while implementation remains limited to app-api source/config/docs and existing UI domain-selector wiring if required.

per_check_results.name: Finalization policy locked to human merge

critic.rationale: The PlanContract is mostly complete for a compact read-only lifecycle-style parity feature: it defines persistence/concurrency protocols, test-first QA, implementation, review, final QA, human-gated finalization, and explicit lifecycle/isolation coverage. The main weakness is slice/path coverage: controller-level Gradle tests are required, but the QA author/verify write scopes only allow tests/ and qa/fixtures/, not app-api/src/test or another clearly Gradle-wired app-api test location. There is also a direct forbidden/allowed overlap between the design slice forbidding qa/fixtures/ and later QA slices allowing qa/fixtures/.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Resolve domain per request without mutable shared controller state or process-wide selected-domain variables. Parallel equities and crypto requests must not contaminate cached identifiers, graph IDs, venues, live config, runtimeConfigVersion, or partition-state payloads across domains.
forbidden_alternatives: Creating /api/diagnostics/crypto/* or other new endpoint families.
Satisfying acceptance by adding new endpoints instead of fixing existing /api/config/* and /api/diagnostics/* behavior.
Duplicating entire controller families when a shared domain-aware projection path exists.
Hard-coding crypto payloads in controllers instead of resolving existing runtime metadata sources.
Using a process-wide selected domain variable.
Patching dag-framework locally.
Adding Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, Drizzle, or any OLTP persistence layer.
Adding snapshot, journal, CRC, or durability machinery for this unrelated read-only parity feature.
hard_constraints: Do not add new diagnostics endpoints.
Do not add config mutation paths.
Do not add app-api writes to Redis, QuestDB, Parquet, SQL, local files, runtime config, or graph state.
Preserve equities payload semantics for domain=equities and omitted-domain calls.
Thread ?domain=crypto through config and diagnostics controllers consistently.
Expose crypto runtimeConfigVersion, graphId, live config, partition state, and domain-correct venue list.
Add selector-switch Playwright coverage for both equities and crypto domains.
Keep the implementation narrow to config and diagnostics parity plus domain-switch coverage.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: app-api owns request-domain parsing, config response projection, and diagnostics response projection. ui owns selector behavior only where existing calls fail to pass or reflect the selected domain. Runtime publishers, Redis, historical stores, app-core, platform-runtime, and crypto-extension remain producers or dependencies and are not modified by this parity pass. QA owns tests/ and qa/fixtures/ only.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: app-api reads existing Redis hot-view and approved historical-store backed runtime metadata only. The feature must not write config, diagnostics, Redis, QuestDB, Parquet, SQL, local files, runtime graph state, or fixtures outside qa/fixtures/.
design_contract.public_api: Existing GET /api/config/* and GET /api/diagnostics/* endpoints accept an optional domain query parameter. For domain=crypto they return crypto runtimeConfigVersion, graphId, live config, partition state, and crypto-correct venues. For domain=equities and omitted-domain calls they preserve existing equities payloads and identifiers. No new endpoints and no mutation routes are added.

final.problem_statement: Implement read-only crypto-domain parity for existing /api/config/* and /api/diagnostics/* endpoints so domain=crypto returns crypto-scoped runtime metadata while domain=equities and omitted-domain calls preserve existing equities behavior.
risk_register: Existing controllers may resolve domain inconsistently across config and diagnostics surfaces, causing partial parity or cross-domain identifier leakage.
Crypto responses may reuse equities defaults through shared helpers unless domain resolution is threaded through every config and diagnostics branch.
Venue lists and graph IDs are high-risk leakage fields because tests may assert shape without checking domain-specific identifiers.
Crypto metadata may be present in Redis hot views under different keys than equities metadata, requiring careful source mapping without hard-coded payloads.
Default-domain behavior may regress if query-param parsing changes globally instead of preserving current equities semantics.
Playwright coverage may pass at the UI layer while backend calls still omit domain unless requests or rendered metadata are asserted.
Read-only constraints could be violated if implementation attempts to create config mutation paths or runtime backfill hooks to manufacture missing crypto metadata.
Over-expanding the slice into new diagnostics routes or persistence work would violate the compact read-only R-003 contract.
